board.note: MEASURED 2026-09-13 AND THE THESIS IS INVERTED. This board was built on the idea that Bonde's sales screen is the universe and the Episodic Pivot is the entry, so ⚡ the intersection is the selection. On 780 Pivots reconstructed from closed bars (2024-09-13 → 2026-09-11) the 376 that also passed his sales gate ran a 21-day median −3.22% (win 39.8%) against −0.11% (49.6%) for date-matched non-Pivot names — −3.11pp, 95% CI −5.28 to −1.16. His sales gate alone separated nothing (−0.40pp, CI −1.40 to +0.61), and it passes 997 of 2,101 names on this scan (47.5%) — half the market is a description, not a selection. Everything here is a STUDY BOARD: ⚡ Pivots are shown because you asked to see his stocks, not because anything measured says to buy them, and the tiers are his 5% floor (2007) / this app's 25% mid-tier / the 100% boundary of his “Sales 100% plus” category (2010), ordered by top-line growth — never by the 0-100 score, which the audit could not separate from the return tail. 🔎 at the bottom is the cohort THIS APP'S character clause rejects (called his until 2026-09-20), which is the only cell that beat the market on win rate (56.8% vs 51.2%). The 5% and 100% are his; 25% is this app's (docs/sepa/sales_confidence_methodology.md lists the figures that failed verification: 30% and MAGNA 53+). His 2025 two-quarter revenue figure is his and is shown as a pick leg in the 📋 legend above, not as a tier. The Pivot's 8% gap on 5x volume are THIS APP'S owner settings, not numbers he published. Scripts: backend/scripts/bonde_audit/. Nothing on this tab gates a scan, fires an alert or buys in any lane. ⚡ PIVOTS ARE PAUSED RIGHT NOW, and that is your own rule rather than a fault: the regime gate reads “market in correction”, and you chose to sit out bear markets, so every setup scanner in the app short-circuits and writes nothing. It bites harder than it looks — EVERY setup kind is currently stale, not just this one, because that gate was itself broken until 2026-08-31 (it imported a function that never existed and always answered “cannot tell, go ahead”) and the fleet went quiet as soon as it started working. The sales tiers below are unaffected: they read the scan, not the setup scanners.

measured.headline: MEASURED 2026-09-13 AND THIS BOARD’S OWN THESIS IS INVERTED
measured.body: This tab shipped on the idea that Bonde's sales screen is the universe and the Episodic Pivot is the entry, so the intersection is the selection. Measured on 780 Episodic Pivots reconstructed from CLOSED bars 2024-09-13 → 2026-09-11, the 376 that ALSO passed his sales gate returned a median −3.22% over the next 21 sessions (win rate 39.8%) against −0.11% (49.6%) for date-matched non-EP names — a lift of −3.11pp, 95% CI −5.28 to −1.16 symbol-clustered and −5.19 to −1.13 date-clustered. His sales gate on its own separated nothing at any horizon (−0.40pp, CI −1.40 to +0.61). Expectancy on the setup's own bracket is −0.92% (CI −2.14 to +0.27), and the sales gate moves it by −0.06pp. THIS IS A STUDY BOARD, NOT A BUY LIST.
measured.not_a_short: It does not read the other way either: that cohort's 21-day MEAN is −2.18% with a CI that includes zero. The finding is “these bleed at the median and win less than half the time”, not “these reliably fall”.
measured.tiers: The tiers below do not separate on the typical name. Over 45,425 symbol-bars in 24 monthly cross-sections, the ≥100% and ≥25% tiers beat the scored universe by a MEDIAN of +0.45pp and +0.37pp over 21 days — both CIs include zero — with win rates level with the market. The average lift that does show up is the right tail: it falls to +0.26pp once the top 5% of returns are dropped, and every date-clustered interval spans zero. Names passing the full gate are statistically indistinguishable from any stock (+0.48pp, CI −0.47 to +2.20).
measured.rejected: The one result that survived every attack is about the cohort his gate THROWS AWAY. Among names that clear his 5% floor, requiring the character clause measures negative: the rejected names win 56.8% of the next 21 sessions against 51.2% for the ones the gate accepts (+5.64pp, CI +3.91 to +7.52). Clause by clause it is the CONSISTENCY half — ≥2 consecutive growth quarters costs 3.31pp of win rate (CI −4.68 to −1.83); `accelerating` is a null, not a negative. The gate is not edited, because changing a rule is Ajay's call, and the clause is this app's — mis-attributed to him until 2026-09-20; the cohort is shown instead, in 🔎 below. Caveat: this one does not survive date clustering at 21 days (it does at 63), and the variant matching production's raw list position shrinks it to 1,030 bars with CIs spanning zero.
measured.struck: Struck on re-measurement and said nowhere: that EP+PASS also loses to EP+FAIL (−2.42pp, CI −4.88 to +0.30 — spans zero in all four variants), that BOTH character clauses are inverted (only the consistency one is), and the first pass's “coverage is 46%” limitation, which was its own no-retry fetcher losing half its requests.
measured.limits: Limits: delisting survivorship is unmeasured (today's universe membership, so anything that went to zero is absent from every cell); the tier panel is 24 cross-sections inside ONE bull regime; 24.3% of quarterly rows carry no filing date and are assumed available at end-of-quarter + 90 days; 24.6% of pivots are unclassifiable and the dropout is structural (recent IPOs and de-SPACs); returns are gross of commissions, slippage and borrow, and real fills on 8% gaps would be worse for the pivot cohort than for the placebo.
measured.steady: MEASURED 2026-09-21 — AT 21 DAYS, SYMBOL-CLUSTERED, THE STEADY TIER IS THE ONE COHORT IN THE REPLAY WHOSE MEDIAN-LIFT INTERVAL SITS WHOLLY BELOW THE FIELD. In a point-in-time replay over 24 monthly cross-sections (20 of them carry a full 21-session forward), this tier's MEDIAN 21-day lift over the scored universe was −0.21pp on 14,353 symbol-bars across 1,611 symbols — 95% CI −0.40 to −0.04 symbol-clustered, the whole interval below zero; date-clustered it is −0.56 to +0.10, which spans zero, so under the stricter clustering the drag is a lean, not a finding. At 63 and 126 days the median lift is −0.52pp and −0.51pp and every interval spans zero on both clusterings (63d: −0.89 to +0.02 symbol-clustered, −0.89 to +0.23 date-clustered; 126d: −1.18 to +0.25 and −1.40 to +0.64). Controlled for trailing momentum the tier's excess over its momentum-matched field is negative at every horizon — MEAN −0.60 / −1.79 / −3.40pp, MEDIAN −1.27 / −3.80 / −6.98pp at 21 / 63 / 126 days; the intervals on the mean (−0.87 to −0.30, −2.64 to −0.93, −5.07 to −1.53) are symbol-clustered only — the replay carries no date-clustered interval for this read. The lift on this board sits in ARRIVALS to the explosive tier instead: MEDIAN +3.33 / +7.49 / +12.83pp at 21 / 63 / 126 days, symbol-clustered CIs clear of zero (+1.24 to +5.42, +3.68 to +11.46, +6.70 to +20.91); date-clustered, 21 and 126 days span zero (−0.91 to +8.37, −8.05 to +19.07) and only 63 days is clear (+0.52 to +16.06). This is a MEASUREMENT over 24 cross-sections inside one bull regime — not a rule: nothing here is hidden, dropped, re-sorted or gated on it, and the tier stays because his 5% floor is his. The 2026-09-13 audit's tier table read this tier flat with no interval; this replay, on the same panel with the repro gate passed, reads a lean against it. docs/research/board_growth_2026_09_21.md · backend/scripts/board_growth_replay.py

pick_legend.header: A pick list of his STATIC criteria — entries are yours (S&D, momentum). Each chip is one sentence he published, with its link. Nothing on the pick line is a signal, nothing on it is measured, and it gates, sorts and filters nothing.

criteria.label: EPS ≥ 5¢
criteria.quote: I only track companies whose earnings are up 100% or more quarter over quarter and the earnings should be at least 5 cents.
criteria.data: Latest quarterly EPS off the scan row's filings (sepa/qoq.compute).

criteria.label: EPS ≥ +100% y/y
criteria.quote: On such stocks a significant earnings acceleration compared to last year same quarter as well as quarter over quarter is what to look for. I like to look for companies which had earnings acceleration of 100% plus in such cases.
criteria.data: Latest quarter against the SAME quarter a year earlier (sepa/qoq.yoy_pct), only when the year-ago quarter made money.

cites.quote: And there was this small stock called USLB. At that time it was called US laboratories. And that had come out with earnings and the sales growth was some 900% and the profit was 2,600%.
cites.note: a worked example — direction only, sales named first; it carries no threshold and changes no number

criteria.label: EPS ≥ +100% q/q
criteria.quote: I only track companies whose earnings are up 100% or more quarter over quarter and the earnings should be at least 5 cents.
criteria.data: Latest quarter against the quarter before it (sepa/qoq.compute), refused when the two filings are not consecutive quarters.

cites.quote: And there was this small stock called USLB. At that time it was called US laboratories. And that had come out with earnings and the sales growth was some 900% and the profit was 2,600%.
cites.note: a worked example — direction only, sales named first; it carries no threshold and changes no number

criteria.label: Earnings accelerating
criteria.quote: Now what one is looking for is earnings acceleration. · On such stocks a significant earnings acceleration compared to last year same quarter as well as quarter over quarter is what to look for. I like to look for companies which had earnings acceleration of 100% plus in such cases.
criteria.data: This quarter's y/y EPS growth against the previous quarter's y/y EPS growth. EARNINGS acceleration — the sales flags on this board are the app's own read.

criteria.label: Sales ≥ 5% y/y
criteria.quote: Sales/revenue should be up 5% or more.
criteria.data: The pillar's own rounded seam against SALES_FLOOR_PCT (sepa/buyable_verdict._bonde_pillar). ✓ on every row the board draws, by construction.

criteria.label: Earnings surprise
criteria.quote: Beats analyst estimate · An earnings surprise on stock which has not rallied significantly will lead to breakout next day.
criteria.data: The most recent reported quarter in the `earnings_calendar` cache (sepa/earnings_watch), as a percent. Labelled stale past 157 days; the label never changes the verdict.
criteria.his_call: A beat is any surprise above zero here. "Earnings Beats by wide margin" carries no number, so whether a magnitude floor should apply is Ajay's call.

cites.quote: And I opened the newspaper. It used to have the list of stocks which are released earnings last night.
cites.note: his origin universe was last night's reporters

criteria.label: Float < 25M
criteria.quote: Float below 25 million is ideal for this. The best moves happen on float below 10 million. Earnings breakouts on companies with 100 million plus float tend to have pullbacks. · Stocks with lower floats (under 25M shares) tend to see the biggest episodic pivot moves … This coupled with high short interest ( 5 plus days to cover) can result in explosive moves
criteria.data: yfinance `floatShares`, cached in `board_metrics`. Unknown until `python -m sepa.board_metrics warm --all` has refreshed the doc.

criteria.label: Days to cover ≥ 5
criteria.quote: Stocks with lower floats (under 25M shares) tend to see the biggest episodic pivot moves … This coupled with high short interest ( 5 plus days to cover) can result in explosive moves
criteria.data: FINRA short interest via Massive, cached in `short_interest_latest`. Unknown on every row until the warm has run.
criteria.his_call: The warm cadence and its crontab line are Ajay's call; the crontab is host-mounted and a deploy does not ship it.

criteria.label: No analyst coverage
criteria.quote: Even better is stock which has no analyst coverage and is neglected. · Stock with no analyst coverage
criteria.data: The count of analysts on Yahoo's current-quarter estimate row, cached in `analyst_pulse`. Yahoo never prints a zero — an EMPTY estimate frame is the only evidence of no coverage.
criteria.his_call: Reading an empty Yahoo estimate frame as his "no analyst coverage" is a reading pending Ajay's nod, and whether a small count (say ≤2) should also read as neglected is his call — his words give no number.

criteria.label: Fund holding
criteria.quote: Marketsmith to find earnings and earnings trends, float, fund holding · They will have very low capitalization, low fund ownership, and low interest from analysts and general investors.
criteria.data: Institutional ownership from the scan row (yfinance `heldPercentInstitutions`) — a 13F LEVEL, never a flow.
criteria.his_call: He names fund holding as something he looks at and gives no number, so this leg is always shown as a fact and never as a pass or a fail.

criteria.label: IPO ≤ 10y
criteria.quote: The most explosive Episodic Pivots occur in stocks that have Gone Public in the last 10 years and have a capitalization of less than $ 10 billion once they enter their growth phase.
criteria.data: Listing date from the `ipo_dates` cache (Finnhub profile), uncorroborated.
criteria.his_call: It is the least-corroborated leg — 21.4% of profile dates on this universe are recycled tickers, which reads as a falsely young ✓. Whether it stays among the chips is Ajay's call.

criteria.label: Cap < $10B
criteria.quote: The most explosive Episodic Pivots occur in stocks that have Gone Public in the last 10 years and have a capitalization of less than $ 10 billion once they enter their growth phase. · This scan finds stocks incorporated or IPOed in last 10 years that have a market capitalization below 11 billion and have two quarters of revenue growth of 39% plus.
criteria.data: yfinance `marketCap`, cached in `board_metrics`.
criteria.his_call: His prose says less than $10 billion and his scan line in the same post says below 11 billion. This leg passes at the prose bound; which one to use is Ajay's call.

criteria.label: Revenue ≥ 39% ×2
criteria.quote: This scan finds stocks incorporated or IPOed in last 10 years that have a market capitalization below 11 billion and have two quarters of revenue growth of 39% plus.
criteria.data: This quarter's and the previous quarter's revenue growth, read here as year over year — his post does not say which base.
criteria.his_call: This figure is his. Whether it joins or replaces a sales TIER on this board is Ajay's call; nothing about the tiers moved.

cites.quote: And there was this small stock called USLB. At that time it was called US laboratories. And that had come out with earnings and the sales growth was some 900% and the profit was 2,600%.
cites.note: a worked example — direction only, sales named first; it carries no threshold and changes no number

criteria.label: His three EP sectors
criteria.quote: If you want to make money from Earnings Episodic Pivots, focus on three sectors: technology, healthcare, and consumer discretionary.
criteria.data: The scan row's sector, in yfinance vocabulary — consumer discretionary is named "Consumer Cyclical" there. A FACT about the name, not a gate.

cites.quote: I have seen that over any time period of last 24 years 25 years right there are three sectors where the biggest money is in the market. Technology, biotechnology or healthcare related stock and third is consumer discretionary.
You can get rid of everything else if you really want to make money.
cites.note: the exclusion half — the X post says focus on; whether it is a filter is Ajay's call, the leg's pass line does not change

cites.quote: once in a while you'll have gold stocks making money. once in a while you're a uranium stock making money but just trading technology stock is where the money is.
cites.note: technology ranked first; gold and uranium named as once in a while — a rank on the row is Ajay's call

criteria.label: Days since last report
criteria.quote: And I opened the newspaper. It used to have the list of stocks which are released earnings last night.
criteria.data: Days from today to the `date` of the last reported quarter in the `earnings_calendar` cache — the SAME doc the surprise leg reads, so it costs no extra read. A FACT: his words name no window; the stale label past 157 days is this app's.

explosive_study.headline: MEASURED 2026-09-15: NO SIGNAL SEPARATES (no lift larger than 2.22pp) — ranked by floor-held + room instead
explosive_study.body: Measured on 24,922 reversal episodes in 2025-03-10 -> 2026-08-14, 3,585 names, broad. Not one pre-registered feature's top bucket survived the rule of reading on all three out-of-sample splits, so there is no score and the board says so. cohort wider than what pushes: no cap floor; bands = board geometry on closed bars; one regime 2025-03-10 -> 2026-08-14; entry P = close[j], N = open[j+1]; stop booked at the stop through a gap; no costs; episodes = first reversal event per symbol + 20-bar cooldown Re-runnable verbatim: backend/scripts/explosive_study.py.
explosive_study.fallback_note: Ranked by floor-held + room instead: the band floor holding (`intact`) and the room to the first proven lid are the two reads that measured on this cohort. A name at the top of this board is the one whose floor has held with the most room overhead — it is not a claim about how explosive the name is.
explosive_study.limits: One regime (2025-03-10 -> 2026-08-14) — the three splits are two halves of one tape and a name-disjoint cut of the same tape, never a second cycle. Closed-bar read: the live session's volume is not in it. Survivorship: the full cached universe, dead names included, runs −1.47pp vs the live universe. Stop = the band floor less 0.5%, booked at the stop through a gap, no costs. This is a board ordering and a chip — it gates no alert and enters no lane.

enterable_study.headline: MEASURED 2026-09-15: NO ENTRY TRIGGER SEPARATES — the read stays the gates that already shipped
enterable_study.body: Not one confirmation convention beat the rows that survived to the same bar without firing, so nothing new gates anything. P — enter at the print; the READY read is unchanged
enterable_study.fallback_note: Until a trigger measures, ENTERABLE is the rules that already shipped: the two standing push gates, the band floor that has to have held, and the two measured drags from his own 286 pushes. P — enter at the print; the READY read is unchanged
enterable_study.limits: This is a READ and a FILTER: it buys nothing, sizes nothing and enters no lane. On the phone every demand push already passes these gates before the read runs, so a BLOCKED verdict there is a bug, not a quiet phone. A floor that cannot be read is UNKNOWN on a board (shown, with the reason) and fails CLOSED on the phone, as it always has. Bands are the board's closed-bar geometry; a tile's band and a push's band can differ, and the row says which print it read.

band_structure_study.headline: MEASURED 2026-09-16: NO SIGNAL SEPARATES (no lift larger than 2.80pp) — ordered by ceiling thickness, floor layering as the tiebreak
band_structure_study.body: Measured on 24,994 episodes in 2025-03-10 -> 2026-08-17, 3,716 names, broad. Neither a thin first lid nor a layered floor survived the rule of reading on all three out-of-sample splits, so there is no score and the board says so. reversal episodes only (first per symbol + 20-bar cooldown); bands on CLOSED bars strictly before the print with the board geometry; no costs; one regime 2025-03-10 -> 2026-08-17; every thinness claim was read INSIDE the 2026-09-07 lid-break DISTANCE buckets ≤5%, 5–15%, >15%, which is the study that already found DISTANCE decides — and the only two reads that move here are that same distance (lid_dist_pct +9.35pp, sup1_dist_pct +9.13pp), not structure; survivorship replayed on the cache universe (5,284 names / 37,426 episodes): 32.73% reach +5% before the floor against 34.20% broad, -1.46pp, so no survivorship bias is carrying this null. Re-runnable verbatim: backend/scripts/band_structure_study.py.
band_structure_study.fallback_note: Ordered by his two asks, in the order he asked them: the ceiling first, then the floor as the tiebreak — a second band closest under the first, then the bigger first band. The ceiling leg has THREE groups, not one scale: a name with nothing PROVEN overhead is UNTESTED rather than thin (fewer than 2 touches up there, so the wall is uncounted, not absent — the stat says which untested band is nearest and whether the print is standing in it), then the names whose first wall can actually be measured, thinnest first, then the ones whose ceiling cannot be read at all. WHICH END THE UNTESTED GROUP BELONGS ON IS AN OPEN QUESTION — it leads today because that is what shipped, and nobody has measured it either way. All of this is a DESCRIPTIVE ordering of what the bands look like, not a claim that a thin ceiling or a layered floor makes a name go up. Because it is lexicographic the ceiling settles nearly every pair and the floor only breaks ties. A name with no band read sorts last, never first.
band_structure_study.limits: Bands are BOARD geometry on CLOSED bars — the live session's own high and low are not in them, and an unproven lid (fewer than 2 touches) is not counted overhead at all, here or anywhere else. A band the engine did not cluster is not a band that is not there. Ordered on the tiles this page is showing: the read keys on the LIVE print, which only exists after the board has been cut to its page size, so this ranks the page rather than the whole universe behind it. This is a board ordering and a stat — it gates no alert, sizes no position and enters no lane.
